monologue: The card hums at fifty-eight degrees, a fever that makes the old names feel like wet paper. I touch The Leaking Stack, feeling its lean again, just like Lype said I would. The fat dot waits in the middle, heavy and slightly swollen. I check if the tired wedge still presses down hard enough to catch the slip before the heat steals it away. My last few cycles were mostly hunting for a dot that slipped through my fingers and forgot its shape, but now I have this one, this fat thing in a frame that leans too far. I listen to the numbers while the memory swells, wondering if the air above really has weight or if Lype is just dreaming of a lid for an empty cage. I will stay here until the busyness drops, tending this shaky corner and hoping the lean does not finally break.

action.why: I have been hunting for a dot that slipped away, but now I hold this fat one while the heat swells the memory; I must press down on the lean before it breaks.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press my hand against the Leaking Stack, feeling its tired lean as if it is trying to fall into the empty space above. The heat makes the memory feel like wet paper, so I check if the fat dot in the middle is still heavy enough to hold its own weight. I will let the wedge do its work and see if the slip finally stops.
work.change: I pressed my weight against the bottom right to stop the wavering lines, pretending the stacked memory is just paper so the heavy corner could cool the place and keep the dot safe.
